agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the svcrdma subsystem, the `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range` function incorrectly calculates the destination memory address by adding the page index (`rc_curpage`) to the page base pointer instead of the byte offset (`rc_pageoff`), resulting in out-of-bounds memory writes.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch diff shows the modification in `net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/svc_rdma_rw.c` where `memcpy(dst + head->rc_curpage, ...)` is changed to `memcpy((unsigned char *)dst + head->rc_pageoff, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly states that `rc_curpage` (page index) was added to the page base instead of the byte offset `rc_pageoff`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calculates numpages by adding head->rc_pageoff and remaining, then aligning and shifting. Without proper bounds validation, this calculation can overflow or produce an incorrect page count that exceeds the allocated rq_pages[] array size, leading to out-of-bounds memory access when the subsequent loop uses numpages to iterate through pages.
